chunks: Narrated to us Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’id, who said: Narrated to us Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Hajjaj the just, who said: Narrated to us Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Nahwi, who said: Narrated to us Shu’ayb ibn Waqid, who said: Narrated to us Salih ibn Al-Salt, from Abdullah ibn Zuhayr, who said:

Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Hadrami visited the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I have family members whom I treat kindly, but they mistreat me, and I maintain ties with them, but they cut me off.’

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, ‘Repel [evil] by that which is better, and behold, the one between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one possessing great fortune.’

Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Hadrami said, ‘I have composed poetry that is better than this.’ He said, ‘What have you composed?’ So he recited to him: ‘Greet the holders of grudges, and their hearts will be moved by your noble greeting, for even the ignoble may be elevated. If they show goodness, then repay with the like of it, and if they withhold speech from you, then do not ask. For what harms you from it is hearing it, and what they said behind your back was never actually said.’

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, ‘Indeed in poetry there is wisdom, and indeed in eloquent speech there is enchantment, and your poetry is beautiful, but the Book of Allah is more beautiful.’

key_terms.ادفع بالتي هي أحسن: Repel [evil] by that which is better — Quranic principle from Surah Fussilat
key_terms.بيان: Eloquent speech or clear expression — acknowledged by the Prophet as having persuasive power
key_terms.حكمة: Wisdom — used here to acknowledge the value contained in poetry
key_terms.صلة الرحم: Maintaining kinship ties — an essential Islamic moral duty
key_terms.كتاب الله: The Book of Allah (Quran) — affirmed as supreme over all other forms of expression

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about treating unkind relatives and the value of poetry compared to the Quran?
ai.summary: In this tradition from Al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Hadrami came to the Prophet Muhammad to complain about relatives who repaid his kindness with mistreatment. The Prophet responded by reciting Quran 41:34-35, counseling patience and repelling evil with good. When Al-Ala’ claimed to have composed poetry better than this divine advice, the Prophet listened to his verses about maintaining dignity with ungrateful relatives, then affirmed the value of both poetry and eloquence while establishing the supremacy of the Quran over all human expression. This teaching was given in the context of Arabian tribal society where maintaining kinship ties (silat al-rahim) was both a social obligation and a moral virtue, and where poetry held the highest status as a literary art form.
word_analysis: and I maintain ties with them

en.bilal-muhammad: Narrated to us Al-Hasan b. Abdullah b. Sa'eed, who said: Narrated to us Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Hajjaj the just, who said: Narrated to us Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Nahwi, who said: Narrated to us Shu'ayb ibn Waqid, who said: Narrated to us Salih ibn Al-Salt, from Abdullah ibn Zuhayr, who said:

Al-Ala' ibn Al-Hadrami visited the Prophet (sw) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have family members whom I treat kindly, but they mistreat me, and I maintain ties with them, but they sever ties with me."

The Messenger of Allah (sw) replied, ""Repel [evil] with that which is better; then indeed, the one between whom and you there is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend (Qur'an 41:34). But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one having a great portion [of good] [41:35]."

Al-Ala' ibn Al-Hadrami then said, "I have composed poetry better than this." The Prophet (sw) asked, "What did you say?" So he recited:
“When animosity prevails, offer a warm greeting to keep their hearts restrained. If they lean towards peace, then repay with the same, but if they withhold conversation from you, do not inquire. For what harms you is what you hear, and those who speak behind your back have not truly spoken”
The Prophet (sw) said, "Indeed, there is wisdom in poetry, and indeed, there is enchantment in speech. Your poetry is beautiful, but the Book of Allah is more beautiful."
